title: Feature Request: Degraded Sensor Warning
body: I realize that many users are extending their sensors well past the warranty period due to financial reasons, but they may be expecting the sensor to outright die before they will replace it leading to prolonged periods of potentially dangerous inaccuracies. Since the Dexcom G6 sensor seems to read low (and I presume other sensors will also read low as they age), I'd suggest displaying a warning message if two successive calibrations are 20 mg/dL higher than what the sensor is reporting. The warning message could say something like "WARNING: Based on your calibration history it appears your sensor is degraded and should be replaced. Failure to replace the sensor now may result in false lows or other dangerous inaccuracies." It may also be worth implementing a clock based reminder at twice the sensor's rated life since I can imagine people who either don't like needles or can't afford test strips trying to extend their sensors indefinitely without calibrations. The clock based alert could say something like "CGM sensors gradually degrade over time. This makes regular calibration increasingly important as sensors age to minimize the risk of false lows and other dangerous inaccuracies."

comments.body:
@definitivequestion No matter how many warnings we add to xDrip, at the end, the only sure safety is provided by the sane judgement of the user.  Without it, no warning will be a remedy.
xDrip is a project.  Anyone who uses a sensor beyond the recommended period, with or without xDrip, is doing so at their own risk and judgement.
